title: Provision S3 Data Lake with IAM Access Controls, Encryption, Lifecycle, CloudTrail, and Bucket Policy

steps.name: Create S3 Data Lake Bucket
steps.description: Provision the primary S3 bucket 'company-datalake-prod' using the community module ~> 4.0. Configure versioning (enabled), server-side encryption (AES-256), block all public access, and lifecycle rule to transition objects to Glacier after 90 days. Apply required tags.
steps.terraform_hint: Use module source 'terraform-aws-modules/s3-bucket/aws' version '~> 4.0'. Key arguments: bucket = 'company-datalake-prod', versioning = { enabled = true }, server_side_encryption_configuration with sse_algorithm = 'AES256', block_public_acls = true, block_public_policy = true, ignore_public_acls = true, restrict_public_buckets = true. Lifecycle rule: id = 'glacier-transition', enabled = true, transition = [{ days = 90, storage_class = 'GLACIER' }]. Tags: Environment = 'prod', Team = 'analytics', CostCenter = 'CC-105'.

steps.name: Apply Bucket Policy Denying Non-HTTPS Requests
steps.description: Attach a bucket policy to 'company-datalake-prod' that denies all requests not made over TLS (aws:SecureTransport = false). This enforces encryption in transit for all bucket operations.
steps.terraform_hint: Use aws_s3_bucket_policy resource. Policy statement: Effect = 'Deny', Principal = '*', Action = 's3:*', Resource = ['arn:aws:s3:::company-datalake-prod', 'arn:aws:s3:::company-datalake-prod/*'], Condition = { Bool = { 'aws:SecureTransport' = 'false' } }.

steps.name: Create IAM Policy for Data Engineers (Read/Write)
steps.description: Create an IAM policy granting read/write access (s3:GetObject, s3:PutObject, s3:DeleteObject, s3:ListBucket, s3:GetBucketLocation, s3:ListBucketMultipartUploadAborts, s3:AbortMultipartUpload) to the data lake bucket. This policy will be attached to the data-engineers IAM role.
steps.terraform_hint: Policy name: 'datalake-data-engineers-rw-policy'. Allow s3:GetObject, s3:PutObject, s3:DeleteObject, s3:ListMultipartUploadParts, s3:AbortMultipartUpload on 'arn:aws:s3:::company-datalake-prod/*' and s3:ListBucket, s3:GetBucketLocation on 'arn:aws:s3:::company-datalake-prod'. Apply tags.

steps.name: Create IAM Policy for Data Analysts (Read-Only)
steps.description: Create an IAM policy granting read-only access (s3:GetObject, s3:ListBucket, s3:GetBucketLocation) to the data lake bucket. This policy will be attached to the data-analysts IAM role.
steps.terraform_hint: Policy name: 'datalake-data-analysts-ro-policy'. Allow s3:GetObject on 'arn:aws:s3:::company-datalake-prod/*' and s3:ListBucket, s3:GetBucketLocation on 'arn:aws:s3:::company-datalake-prod'. Apply tags.

steps.name: Create IAM Role for Data Engineers
steps.description: Create an IAM role 'datalake-data-engineers-role' that the data-engineers team can assume. The trust policy allows principals in account 123456789012 to assume this role. Tagged appropriately.
steps.terraform_hint: Role name: 'datalake-data-engineers-role'. Assume role policy: allow sts:AssumeRole from account root 'arn:aws:iam::123456789012:root' (refine trust to specific IdP/group post-deploy). Apply tags: Environment = 'prod', Team = 'analytics', CostCenter = 'CC-105'.

steps.name: Create IAM Role for Data Analysts
steps.description: Create an IAM role 'datalake-data-analysts-role' that the data-analysts team can assume. The trust policy allows principals in account 123456789012 to assume this role. Tagged appropriately.
steps.terraform_hint: Role name: 'datalake-data-analysts-role'. Assume role policy: allow sts:AssumeRole from account root 'arn:aws:iam::123456789012:root'. Apply tags: Environment = 'prod', Team = 'analytics', CostCenter = 'CC-105'.

steps.name: Attach Read/Write Policy to Data Engineers Role
steps.description: Attach the data-engineers read/write IAM policy to the data-engineers IAM role, granting the team full read/write access to the data lake bucket.
steps.terraform_hint: Use aws_iam_role_policy_attachment. role = aws_iam_role.data_engineers.name, policy_arn = aws_iam_policy.data_engineers_rw.arn.

steps.name: Attach Read-Only Policy to Data Analysts Role
steps.description: Attach the data-analysts read-only IAM policy to the data-analysts IAM role, granting the team read-only access to the data lake bucket.
steps.terraform_hint: Use aws_iam_role_policy_attachment. role = aws_iam_role.data_analysts.name, policy_arn = aws_iam_policy.data_analysts_ro.arn.

steps.name: Create CloudTrail Logging S3 Bucket
steps.description: Create a dedicated S3 bucket 'company-datalake-prod-cloudtrail-logs' to store CloudTrail log files. CloudTrail requires a separate bucket for log delivery. Versioning and encryption enabled, all public access blocked.
steps.terraform_hint: Bucket name: 'company-datalake-prod-cloudtrail-logs'. Enable versioning, AES-256 SSE, block all public access. Apply tags. This is a plain aws_s3_bucket + aws_s3_bucket_versioning + aws_s3_bucket_server_side_encryption_configuration + aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block (or use the same community module).

steps.name: Apply Bucket Policy for CloudTrail Log Delivery
steps.description: Attach a bucket policy to the CloudTrail logging bucket that allows the CloudTrail service to write log files (s3:PutObject) and check bucket ACL (s3:GetBucketAcl).
steps.terraform_hint: Allow Principal 'cloudtrail.amazonaws.com' actions s3:GetBucketAcl on bucket ARN and s3:PutObject on bucket ARN/* with condition StringEquals 's3:x-amz-acl' = 'bucket-owner-full-control'. Also enforce aws:SourceArn matching the trail ARN.

steps.name: Create CloudTrail Trail with S3 Data Events
steps.description: Create a CloudTrail trail 'datalake-prod-trail' that logs S3 data events (GetObject, PutObject, DeleteObject) for the 'company-datalake-prod' bucket. Logs are delivered to the dedicated CloudTrail logging bucket. This provides an audit trail for all data lake access.
steps.terraform_hint: Trail name: 'datalake-prod-trail'. s3_bucket_name = CloudTrail logging bucket. is_multi_region_trail = false. enable_logging = true. event_selector block: read_write_type = 'All', include_management_events = false, data_resource type = 'AWS::S3::Object', values = ['arn:aws:s3:::company-datalake-prod/']. Apply tags.

planner_notes:
Assumptions & Notes:
1. Region is us-east-1, AWS account 123456789012 as specified.
2. The S3 bucket module terraform-aws-modules/s3-bucket/aws ~> 4.0 is used for the bucket itself (step_01). Versioning, encryption (AES-256), public access block, and lifecycle rules are configured within the module invocation. A separate aws_s3_bucket_policy resource is used for the HTTPS-deny policy since it is cleaner to manage independently.
3. IAM roles assume that the data-engineers and data-analysts teams will assume these roles. Trust policies are created with the current account as principal; the requester should refine the trust relationship (e.g., specific SAML provider, SSO, or IAM users/groups) post-provisioning.
4. CloudTrail is configured for S3 data events on the target bucket. A dedicated CloudTrail trail is created with a separate logging S3 bucket to store trail logs (required by CloudTrail). The logging bucket has its own policy to allow CloudTrail to write.
5. All resources are tagged: Environment=prod, Team=analytics, CostCenter=CC-105.
6. Naming conventions: IAM roles prefixed with 'datalake-', CloudTrail trail named 'datalake-prod-trail', logging bucket named 'company-datalake-prod-cloudtrail-logs'.
7. Risk: The bucket name 'company-datalake-prod' must be globally unique; if taken, the apply will fail.
